source: Being gratuitously harmful is sufficient for this intervention to be wrong. This intervention is gratuitously harmful. Therefore this intervention is wrong.

reconstruction.title: Argument Against the Intervention Based on Gratuitous Harm

claims.text: Being gratuitously harmful is sufficient for this intervention to be wrong.

evidence.quote: Being gratuitously harmful is sufficient for this intervention to be wrong.

claims.interpretation_note: States a general sufficient condition for wrongness.
Asserts the specific case meets the sufficient condition.
Directly follows from the two premises via modus ponens.

translations.reason: The first premise establishes a sufficient condition: if G (gratuitous harm) then W (wrongness).
Direct assertion of the antecedent condition in the specific case.
Conclusion derived via modus ponens from (implies G W) and G.

interpretation_notes: The argument uses material implication to model sufficiency. No first-order quantifiers are needed since the scope is a single specific intervention.
Modus ponens applies directly: (G → W) ∧ G ⊢ W
